children: The Investment & Development Conversations session, titled ‘Capital, Confidence & Capacity: Funding India's Hospitality Future’, brought together leaders from investment, development and hotel ownership to discuss the capital, capacity and partnerships shaping the next phase of India’s hospitality sector

The 10th edition of the prestigious BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026), hosted at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity, is bringing leading voices from across the hospitality industry for the next two days of conversations on the sector’s growth and evolution. With the theme
‘India’s Hospitality Decade: From Growth to Greatness’
, the Summit will examine the opportunities, challenges and shifts shaping India’s hospitality landscape as the industry enters a defining decade.
The
Investment & Development Conversations
session, titled
‘Capital, Confidence & Capacity: Funding India's Hospitality Future’
, brought together leaders from investment, development and hotel ownership to discuss the capital, capacity and partnerships shaping the next phase of India’s hospitality sector.
The conversation was chaired by
Gaurav Sharma, Head of Hotels & Hospitality Group for India & Sr. Director, Hotel Capital Markets, JLL
, with

Ashank Kothari, MD, Real Estate Group, Brookfield Asset Management; Balvinder Sahrawat, VP – Development -South Asia, Accor; Dhruva Rathore, VP – Development, India & Southwest Asia, Hyatt; Rahul Pandit, MD & CEO, Advent Hotels International; and Rahul Chaudhary, MD & CEO, CG Hospitality

Sharma addressed, “The two decades of my life have been a new journey for me. When new investments started coming into real estate, Indian hospitality found its way into those opportunities. Today, the demand is growing, travel is growing and new destinations are emerging, but everyone is asking about the hotels. JLL has completed eight hospitality transactions in about eight months, reflecting the growing activity in India’s hospitality investment market.”
Kothari quoted, “Your rent resets every day and starts fresh, making hospitality a unique real estate asset class where pricing can respond dynamically to market demand.”

Sahrawat explained, “Everyone is in the race to build a big hotel, not the best hotel. The focus should be on building the right product for the market rather than simply pursuing scale. The moment cost accounting comes in, financial viability goes for a toss, which makes it important to assess the economics of a project carefully from the outset.”

Rathore emphasised, “Being honest with the owner is the first and most important thing to follow when you enter into a partnership. Getting alignment with the owner and being constructive in decision-making is key to building strong partnerships.”

Pandit said, “For a developer, it’s important to do an assessment even before the planning process. When we are doing development, it’s important to balance the structure and ensure that the project is aligned with its requirements.”
Chaudhary addressed, “We never see investments from our ego; investments are always seen from the perspective of returns. We are more directly involved in the wellness space.”

As the discussion drew to a close, speakers focussed on the friction points between project conception and real-world delivery. The consensus was that scaling quality supply across emerging destinations relies on operators offering adaptable brand standards, while developers adopt sharper build practices that protect owner capital during long construction cycles.

The two-day BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) encompasses over 25 sessions where hospitality veterans and experts across the nation gathered to provide diverse knowledge and insights. The Summit & Awards is a testament to BW Hotelier’s commitment towards revolutionising Indian hospitality by honouring the crème de la crème of the industry.
